stem: Who introduced ‘Do-aspa and Sih-aspa’ system?
expl: ‘Do-aspa and Sih-aspa’ system was introduced by Jahangir. Under the provision of this system, Mansabdars had to maintain an excess number of soldiers without increment in rank (zat). Do-aspa : In this system, Mansabdars had to maintain double horses in comparison to their ‘Sawar’ rank. Sih-aspa : In this system, Mansabdars had to maintain a triple number of horses in comparison to their ‘Sawar’ rank.

stem: Mughal painting reached its zenith under :
expl: The Mughal painting reached its zenith under the reign of Jahangir. Earlier, the paintings were concerned with the contents of manuscripts, but Jahangir freed it from this bondage. Ustad Mansur was specialized in depicting plants and animals while Abul Hasan was a portrait artist.

stem: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
expl: Jahangir was an outstanding author as well as a critic. He wrote his autobiography in Persian language and named it Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri. Jahangir had recorded his merits as well as demerits in his autobiography. This memoir has been divided into three parts. The fi rst part is the preface which was written by Muhammad Hadi after the death of Jahangir in which the early life of Jahangir is mentioned. The second part was an original piece of text narrated by Jahangir. The third part of the text was written by Muhammad Hadi. Babur wrote his autobiography ‘Tuzuk-i-Babri’’ in the Turkish language.

stem: Itmad-ud-Daula’s tomb at Agra was built by
expl: Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula was built by Nur Jahan at Agra between 1622-1628 A.D. after the death of her father. This elegant monument is located on the left bank of river Yamuna. The main mausoleum is built with white marble. Itmad-ud-Daula has a special place in the chronicles of both history as well as architecture. The monument is priceless because this is the fi rst tomb in India that is entirely made up of white marble. In spite of marble and inlay work, it was for the fi rst time when a new style of ornamentation, Pietradura, was used.
